title: How can tax and finance leaders prepare their function for an AI-enabled future?
gist: Oxford Economics and EY surveyed 1,600 tax and finance executives across 22 industries and conclude AI can create capacity for tax/finance functions facing rising regulatory and geopolitical complexity, but technology alone won't deliver transformation without trusted data and human judgement. Teaser page; full findings gated.

themes.theme: AI in tax and finance functions

insights.claim: An Oxford Economics–EY survey of 1,600 tax and finance executives across 22 industries finds that transforming tax and finance requires more than applying AI to existing processes.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Enterprise AI value in finance depends on process redesign, which favors consultancies and workflow vendors over pure model providers.
insights.quote: Transforming tax and finance requires more than applying AI to existing processes.
insights.locator: Transforming tax and finance requires more

insights.claim: Geopolitical instability, shifting trade policies and the expansion of digital tax administration are increasing compliance complexity and pressure on corporate tax and finance teams.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Rising compliance burden is a demand driver for tax-tech and compliance automation software.
insights.locator: Amidst geopolitical instability, shifting trade policies

insights.claim: The Oxford Economics–EY research concludes AI can create the capacity tax and finance functions need to take on strategic risk-identification roles, but technology alone will not deliver transformation without trusted data and human judgement.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Expect enterprise AI adoption in finance to be gated by data quality and governance, slowing realized productivity gains.
insights.quote: AI can help create the capacity needed to meet these expectations, but technology alone will not deliver transformation
